\section[taṇuppŭ]{\ml{തണുപ്പ്} (taṇuppŭ) — cold (weather)}

\label{lesson:ML-C118-coldweather}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for vomiting, then the Malayalam for a wound.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{തണുപ്പ്}}
\textbf{\ml{തണുപ്പ്}} (\emph{taṇuppŭ}) — \textquotedblleft{}cold\textquotedblright{}, the cold of the weather rather than the illness \textbf{\ml{ജലദോഷം}}. \textbf{\ml{നല്ല} \ml{തണുപ്പ്}} — \textquotedblleft{}it's really cold\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The cold you feel outside.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taṇuppŭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taṇuppŭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nalla taṇuppŭ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for vomiting, then the Malayalam for a wound, then say \emph{taṇuppŭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{തണുപ്പ്} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Cold (weather)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[cūṭŭ]{\ml{ചൂട്} (cūṭŭ) — heat}

\label{lesson:ML-C118-heat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a wound, then the Malayalam for the cold.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ചൂട്}}
\textbf{\ml{ചൂട്}} (\emph{cūṭŭ}) — \textquotedblleft{}heat\textquotedblright{}, and also \textquotedblleft{}hot\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ml{നല്ല} \ml{ചൂട്}} — \textquotedblleft{}it's really hot\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The opposite of taṇuppŭ.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cūṭŭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cūṭŭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nalla cūṭŭ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a wound, then the Malayalam for the cold, then say \emph{cūṭŭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ചൂട്} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Heat\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[uṟakkaṁ]{\ml{ഉറക്കം} (uṟakkaṁ) — sleep, sleepiness}

\label{lesson:ML-C118-sleep}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for the cold, then the Malayalam for heat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഉറക്കം}}
\textbf{\ml{ഉറക്കം}} (\emph{uṟakkaṁ}) — \textquotedblleft{}sleep\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ml{എനിക്ക്} \ml{ഉറക്കം} \ml{വരുന്നു}} — \textquotedblleft{}I'm getting sleepy\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}sleep is coming to me\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Sleep arrives, in Malayalam.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uṟakkaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uṟakkaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{enikkŭ uṟakkaṁ varunnu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for the cold, then the Malayalam for heat, then say \emph{uṟakkaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഉറക്കം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Sleep, sleepiness\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[maññŭ]{\ml{മഞ്ഞ്} (maññŭ) — mist, dew, snow}

\label{lesson:ML-C118-mist}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for heat, then the Malayalam for sleep.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{മഞ്ഞ്}}
\textbf{\ml{മഞ്ഞ്}} (\emph{maññŭ}) — \textquotedblleft{}mist, dew\textquotedblright{}, and the word for snow too. Kerala's hills have the mist.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Cool weather's word.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maññŭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maññŭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{maññŭ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for heat, then the Malayalam for sleep, then say \emph{maññŭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{മഞ്ഞ്} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Mist, dew, snow\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[iṭiminnal]{\ml{ഇടിമിന്നൽ} (iṭiminnal) — thunder and lightning}

\label{lesson:ML-C118-thunder}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for sleep, then the Malayalam for mist.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഇടിമിന്നൽ}}
\textbf{\ml{ഇടിമിന്നൽ}} (\emph{iṭiminnal}) — \textquotedblleft{}thunder and lightning\textquotedblright{}: \textbf{\ml{ഇടി}} (\emph{iṭi}), \textquotedblleft{}thunder\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ml{മിന്നൽ}} (\emph{minnal}), \textquotedblleft{}lightning\textquotedblright{}. The monsoon brings both.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Two storm words in one.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṭiminnal}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṭiminnal}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{iṭiminnal}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for sleep, then the Malayalam for mist, then say \emph{iṭiminnal} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഇടിമിന്നൽ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Thunder and lightning\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
